worked: Federal AGI = wages 50,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 34,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 50,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 50,000.00 - 0.00 = 50,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 50,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 50,000.00 is more than 44,000.00, exemption 0.00; Line 3 taxable income = 50,000.00 - 0.00 = 50,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 50,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 + 40,000.00 x 0.045 = 200.00 + 1,800.00 = 2,000.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 50,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 2,000.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 50,000.00 is in the band more than 33,300.00); Line 9 = 2,000.00 x 0.10 = 200.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 2,000.00 - 200.00 = 1,800.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut AGI 50,000 is past the end of the single exemption phase-out (44,000 and up: 0).
